subject: Burst absorber & egress affinity — private GPU pool throughput plan
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgelabs.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Burst absorber & egress affinity — private GPU pool throughput plan

Team / Sanjay —

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is a compact plan that captures the capacity profile we need for the initial private GPU pool we will co-locate with EdgeLabs. High-level objectives:

- Sustained throughput target: 100k tokens/min (customer-facing steady-state)
- Burst runway: absorb up to 300k tokens/min for a 10-minute window (safety margin for marketing / flash events)
- Latency SLO: p90 < 300ms for standard generation flows; p99 mitigation via admission control
- Network constraints: egress affinity so traffic with large model state stays within the same cross-connect to avoid duplicate egress and keep tail latency predictable

What I attached: a traffic matrix (burst-traffic-matrix.xlsx) with per-customer concurrency profiles and an egress affinity diagram (egress-affinity-diagram.png). Please treat the matrix as our working numbers — we can tune after the soak test.

Asks / next steps:
1) Jonas — can you review the hardware tiling proposal and confirm the warm-pool sizing and admission control knobs we discussed? See the quick bullets in the matrix.
2) David — confirm cross-connect and NIC sizing for 40Gbps host links / aggregate 100Gbps uplink assumptions.
3) Sanjay — confirm rack/cage availability and lead time for a 10U cage with direct cross-connect. Also propose a week for a 48h soak.
4) Laura — heads-up on procurement lead times and whether we need to open a CapEx request for the reserve nodes.

I put a short timeline in the deck: hardware order week of 22 Mar, install week of 19 Apr, soak test week of 26 Apr. If anyone needs a different cadence speak up.

Thanks —
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgelabs.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Burst absorber & egress affinity — private GPU pool throughput plan

Mina — good summary. I ran the numbers against our recent kernel profiles and the attached sizing notes (mcap-sizing-notes.pdf). Short version below; details in the PDF.

Sizing recommendation (initial pool):
- Base tile: 8 x A100-80GB hosts (shared across tenants) — supports ~100k tokens/min sustained at target latency with batching tuned to 32 tokens average and continuous KV prefix caching enabled.
- Warm absorber: 4 x A100-80GB (kept warm with periodic health traffic) to handle 2.5x bursts to ~300k tokens/min for up to 10 minutes without harming steady-state throughput. Warm pool operates with reduced batching to limit queueing latency.
- Headroom: reserve 25% compute headroom (admission control) to avoid cascade failure under tail events.

Networking & placement: 
- Host NIC: 40Gbps per host (recommended Mellanox ConnectX-6), cross-connect to EdgeLabs fabric with 100Gbps uplink aggregation. For the tile above, expected egress consumption at peak burst ~85Gbps (compressed token payloads + model fetch traffic).
- Egress affinity: pin long-running model sessions to the same host group and ensure return traffic uses the same cross-connect to avoid hairpinning through external routers; the affinity table is in the diagram.

Operational knobs:
- Admission control: dynamic token-budget per-customer, soft-queue with backpressure at 90th percentile.
- Batch tuning: auto-batching up to 64 for background workloads, capped at 16 for interactive sessions.
- Warm-pool warming: heartbeat at 30s, synthetic token streams during idle windows.

Open items for decision:
1) Tolerable headroom fraction — I recommended 25% but we can lower to 15% if procurement lead times are prohibitive.
2) Warm-pool sizing vs. cost — tradeoff between extra hosts vs. slightly higher admission rates during bursts.

If this looks good I will convert the PDF into a short slide for legal/procurement.

Jonas

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Burst absorber & egress affinity — private GPU pool throughput plan

Mina / all —

Thanks, looks sensible from a delivery perspective. A few procurement/contract notes:

- Lead times: A100 procurement + rack provisioning in EdgeLabs colo is ~6-8 weeks once we raise PO. If we want install week of 19 Apr we'll need an approved PO by 22 Mar (tight).
- Budget: the warm-absorber hosts will push this into a mid-size CapEx line; I'll prepare a CapEx request template and flag the business justification (flash-event protection + SLA).
- Contract: add a clause describing egress affinity constraints and cross-connect SLA (latency + packet loss), otherwise egress costs and tail behavior may shift to EdgeLabs. Sanjay—please confirm you can include a cross-connect SLA attachment.

Operational ask: include a 48-hour soak with the following pass/fail criteria: stable p90 latency within 10% of baseline, no admission-control-triggered failures for steady-state traffic, and warm-pool hit rate > 80% during simulated bursts.

I'll kick the CapEx draft today and loop in finance if Jonas confirms the final host counts.

Laura

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Burst absorber & egress affinity — private GPU pool throughput plan

Mina / team —

Thanks for the clear plan. EdgeLabs can accommodate a 10U cage with a single 100Gbps cross-connect and per-host 40Gbps NICs. We can commit to: 

- Rack availability: 3 weeks lead after PO (hardware lead still on Redwood)
- Cross-connect SLA: 99.95% with <1% packet loss target on our internal fabric — we will attach a formal SLA to the contract (draft by Tue EOD).
- Soak test: week of 26 Apr works for us; we can reserve Apr 27-28 for the 48h soak and provide an infra engineer on-call.

Two notes from infra:
1) We will run the soak behind a traffic-shaper that can emulate global bursts (we will provide waveforms). Please confirm the warm-pool heartbeats and synthetic streams will not be blocked by our traffic shaper.
2) Egress affinity: we support sticky routes on the EdgeLabs fabric but require a short TTL (60s) for affinity entries. That means long sessions should refresh every 60s to keep the slot. Is that acceptable?

If yes to both, consider this an agreement in principle from EdgeLabs. I will send the SLA draft and infra contact off-line.

— Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure, EdgeLabs Inc
